subject: Data Science
report_status: FINAL - answer correctness, citation support and groundedness were suggested by an AI assistant, then reviewed and confirmed by the group (2026-10-17). Instructor review still pending.

test_conditions.hardware: Acer TravelMate P215-54, Intel Core i7-1255U, 12 GB RAM, integrated graphics only (CPU inference), Windows 11
test_conditions.benchmark: 30 questions: 10 validation, 20 held-out test. 6 categories. Questions and reference answers were drafted with an AI assistant and need review by the group and instructor; expected evidence pages were labelled by the group with AI-suggested labels that the group reviewed.
test_conditions.note_on_recall: Recall@5 is measured with plain retrieval (no book filtering). The chatbot itself filters by named books, so cross-book retrieval in the app is better than the Recall@5 figure suggests.
test_conditions.answer_review: Each answer was marked yes / partly / no against the reference answer. Marks were first suggested by an AI assistant, then reviewed and confirmed by the group.

extraction_issues: ISLR PDF pages 146, 282, 284 and 290 are plots whose tick marks were extracted as long runs of '| | |'. They produced 211 junk chunks (141 from page 146 alone).
Equations in maths-heavy books (Bishop, MML, Convex Optimization, UML) are flattened into plain text, which loses structure.
Citations use PDF page numbers, not printed page numbers.
document_processing.metadata_completeness: All 14 manifest entries have title, author, edition, publisher, year, source URL and permission status. ISBN fields are empty.

test.peak_system_ram: about 93% of 12 GB (~11.2 GB) for the whole system during the test run; per-process RAM not recorded

validation_tuning_history.change: stricter refusal rule; search by topic with book names removed; drop weak passages from named books
rule-based refusal for time-sensitive questions (latest, current, today) before generation

failures_and_error_analysis.finding: The 3B model gets calculations wrong even when the right formula is retrieved (Q018). For Q016 and Q017 no retrieved passage contained the answer; the model copied nearby numbers (1/4, 1/2).
'Transformers' matched OpenIntro's 'transformations' (log rescaling), so the chatbot answered instead of refusing.
'Why' questions retrieve on-topic passages that do not contain the explanation; D2L's section comparing CNNs, RNNs and attention was not retrieved.
Without book filtering one book's passages crowd out the other. Book filtering in the chatbot fixes retrieval, but the model still sometimes attributes a claim to the wrong book (Q022, Q023).
Q009 retrieved a web-link 'inverted index' table instead of the term index; during labelling, 'bias' also matched the intercept term in D2L.
Some sentences carry no citation despite the prompt rule; long answers (Q021, Q022) are cut off by the 300-token limit.

limitations: Small 3B model on CPU: weak arithmetic and comparison reasoning; cross-book answers take 35-46 s.
Time-sensitive refusal is a keyword rule, not learned behaviour.
Only 30 benchmark questions (20 test), so each test question moves a metric by 5-25 percentage points.
Citations point to PDF pages, not printed pages.
Junk chunks from plot pages remain in the index.
Embedding model and group ID are placeholders until the coordinator confirms them; changing them requires rebuilding the index and rerunning the evaluation.
Answer correctness was reviewed by the group, not yet by the instructor or a subject expert.
